title: Stability integration runway — cross-functional sprint sketch
body:
Summary:
A compact, 6-week sketch for a cross-functional stability sprint focused on integrating new SLO signals into the platform routing and alerting pipelines. Purpose is to get a minimally viable runway: instrumentation -> small experiment -> rollback/fallback policy -> handoff checklist. This is intentionally lightweight: emphasis on clear owner handoffs and measurable, reversible changes.

Goals (measurable):
- Instrument top 5 model-serving routes with end-to-end latency and KV-cache hit-rate signals by end of week 2. (metric targets: 95th latency, cache hit %)
- Run two small canaries that exercise traffic shaping and model-variant fallback for degraded capacity by week 4.
- Define SLO burn-to-action mapping and oncall playbook; have a one-page handoff doc ready for feature teams by week 6.

Hypothesis to test:
If we add lightweight route-level prefix caching telemetry and tie signal thresholds to automated routing adjustments, then end-user P95 latency will improve under bursty loads and the number of manual escalations will drop.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Platform lead: Priya Kapoor (overall owner)
- Observability: Liam Chen (instrumentation & dashboards)
- Serving runtime: Marcus Lee (model-fallback wiring)
- Product/Console: Sofia Alvarez (UI visibility + rollouts)
- SRE liaison: Casey Morgan (oncall & playbook)
- Feature team beta partners: Search-team (owner: Mina Patel)

Sprint structure (6 weeks):
Week 0 (preparatory):
- Alignment sync with SRE, runtime, product (Priya)
- Inventory: list top 20 routes by qps and select top 5 candidates (Liam + Mina)
- Quick dependency scan: KMS, routing policy store, metrics DB cost estimate (Marcus)

Week 1–2 (instrumentation & dashboarding):
- Add prefix/KV cache hit metrics and per-route queuing latency to telemetry (Liam + Marcus)
- Lightweight dashboard templates (P95/P99 latencies, error rate, cache hit) in Console (Sofia)
- Smoke tests and synthetic traffic harness for target routes (Mina + SRE)

Week 3–4 (experiment wiring & canaries):
- Implement a traffic-shaping experiment framework toggle: gradual ramp with 5% -> 25% -> 50% steps (Marcus)
- Create a fallback-to-quantized-model policy for constrained capacity (Marcus + runtime)
- Run two canaries: one latency-focused, one fallback-focused (Feature team + SRE)

Week 5 (runbook and decision mapping):
- Formalize burn-rate mappings: what actions at <10m, 10–60m, >60m sustained SLO burn
- Draft one-page oncall playbook and escalation matrix (Casey + Priya)
- Collect RB metrics from canaries and produce short retrospective notes (Liam)

Week 6 (handoff & ops):
- Handoff doc to feature teams + product (Sofia)
- Postmortem / lessons learned & next steps (all)
- Decide on rollout cadence for remaining routes (Priya)

Dependencies / assumptions:
- Metrics DB can accept additional high-cardinality tagging for 5 routes (ops cost TBD).
- Serving runtime has a safe mechanism to swap model variants in-flight without client-visible failures (requires one runtime PR: see linked PR).
- Teams will have 2–4 hours/week available for coordination (assume small beta).

Quick risk heatmap (likelihood x impact):
- Increased metrics cost (med x med) -> early gating: limit cardinality, sample at 10% if necessary.
- Canary causes increased error chatter (low x high) -> run in isolated tenant + automatic rollback.
- Ambiguous SLO actions -> mitigate by explicit burn-to-action matrix; keep actions reversible.

Acceptance criteria (end of 6 weeks):
- Dashboards show clean baseline + canary traces for top 5 routes.
- At least one canary demonstrates safe fallback without client-visible failure.
- Oncall playbook exists and SRE can run a 30-minute drill using it.

Communication plan and rituals:
- Twice-weekly 30m sync: Tue/Thu (standup + unblock). Owner: Priya.
- Weekly written micro-update (released on Wed) with 3 bullets: progress, blockers, requests. Owner: Liam.
- Slack channel: #stability-runway (use for quick questions and canary telemetry alerts).

Practical checklist (TODOs):
- [ ] Create synthetic traffic templates for the 5 routes (Mina)
- [ ] Instrument cache-hit and per-route queue time (Liam)
- [ ] Add dashboard widgets to Console (Sofia)
- [ ] Implement toggled traffic shaping with automatic rollback (Marcus)
- [ ] Draft one-page playbook and run a tabletop drill (Casey)

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Do we need a short retention policy for the new telemetry to control cost? (ask cost-ops)
- Should canaries use real customer traffic or synthetic proxies? (prefers synthetic for initial run)
- How to signal model-quality regressions vs infra regressions when fallback occurs? (investigate coupling of eval signals)

Next concrete steps this week:
1) Alignment session Wed 2026-01-21 10:00am PT — sync owners and confirm top-5 routes. (Priya)
2) Liam to sketch dashboard and post link to #stability-runway by Fri 2026-01-23.
3) Marcus to open minimal PR for traffic shaping toggle (target: branch + doc) by Mon 2026-01-26.

Appendix (short):
- Minimal burn-to-action mapping (example):
  * <5% burn: monitor
  * 5–20% sustained over 30m: scale routing weight away from impacted cluster and alert SRE
  * >20% sustained over 60m: automated fallback to lower-capacity model variant and page oncall

Notes: this doc is purposely lightweight and iterative. The objective is to create a repeatable pattern ("runway") the platform team can replicate for other route groups without heavy upfront governance. Keep small, measurable, and reversible.
